review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

15:1.sourceText: Ἦσαν δὲ αὐτῷ ἐγγίζοντες πάντες οἱ τελῶναι καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ.
15:1.targetText: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were gathering around to listen to Jesus.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτοῦ (him) is rendered with the name Jesus.

unmappedSource.reason: The dative αὐτῷ (to him) is left implicit in gathering around.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:2.sourceText: καὶ διεγόγγυζον οἵ τε Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς λέγοντες ὅτι Οὗτος ἁμαρτωλοὺς προσδέχεται καὶ συνεσθίει αὐτοῖς.
15:2.targetText: So the Pharisees and scribes began to grumble: “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”

groups.note: The imperfect διεγόγγυζον (were grumbling) is rendered began to grumble.

unmappedSource.reason: τε pairs with καί (both … and); BSB renders only and.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
λέγοντες ("saying") is represented by the colon and quotation marks.
ὅτι introduces the direct quotation and is represented by the quotation marks.

15:3.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην λέγων
15:3.targetText: Then Jesus told them this parable:

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The participle λέγων ("saying") introducing the parable is represented by the colon.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject that the Greek verb ending implies.

15:4.sourceText: Τίς ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ὑμῶν ἔχων ἑκατὸν πρόβατα καὶ ἀπολέσας ἐξ αὐτῶν ἓν οὐ καταλείπει τὰ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ καὶ πορεύεται ἐπὶ τὸ ἀπολωλὸς ἕως εὕρῃ αὐτό;
15:4.targetText: “What man among you, if he has a hundred sheep and loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the pasture and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it?

groups.note: The participle ἔχων (having) is rendered as a condition.
ἐρήμῳ (wilderness, open country) is rendered pasture.

15:5.sourceText: καὶ εὑρὼν ἐπιτίθησιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὤμους αὐτοῦ χαίρων,
15:5.targetText: And when he finds it, he joyfully puts it on his shoulders,

groups.note: The participle χαίρων (rejoicing) is rendered joyfully.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for finds; the Greek participle has none.
English supplies an object for puts; the Greek has none.

15:6.sourceText: καὶ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὸν οἶκον συνκαλεῖ τοὺς φίλους καὶ τοὺς γείτονας, λέγων αὐτοῖς Συνχάρητέ μοι, ὅτι εὗρον τὸ πρόβατόν μου τὸ ἀπολωλός.
15:6.targetText: comes home, and calls together his friends and neighbors to tell them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost sheep!’

groups.note: The καί joining puts (15:5) and calls is rendered by the and of BSB's list.
εἰς τὸν οἶκον (into the house) is rendered home.
The participle λέγων (saying) is rendered to tell.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:7.sourceText: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὕτως χαρὰ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἔσται ἐπὶ ἑνὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ μετανοοῦντι ἢ ἐπὶ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα δικαίοις οἵτινες οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν μετανοίας.
15:7.targetText: In the same way, I tell you that there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous ones who do not need to repent.

groups.note: ἤ (rather than) after joy expresses the comparison, rendered more … than.
χρείαν ἔχουσιν (have need) is rendered need.
The noun μετανοίας (of repentance) is rendered to repent.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:8.sourceText: Ἢ τίς γυνὴ δραχμὰς ἔχουσα δέκα, ἐὰν ἀπολέσῃ δραχμὴν μίαν, οὐχὶ ἅπτει λύχνον καὶ σαροῖ τὴν οἰκίαν καὶ ζητεῖ ἐπιμελῶς ἕως οὗ εὕρῃ;
15:8.targetText: Or what woman who has ten silver coins and loses one of them does not light a lamp, sweep her house, and search carefully until she finds it?

groups.note: δραχμάς (drachmas) is rendered silver coins.
δραχμήν (a drachma) is rendered of them, referring back to the coins.

unmappedSource.reason: The conditional ἐάν (if) is not rendered; BSB recasts the condition as who has … and loses.
The first καί is represented by the comma in BSB's list.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins loses to has in the relative clause; ἐάν means if, not and.
English supplies an object for finds; the Greek has none.

15:9.sourceText: καὶ εὑροῦσα συνκαλεῖ τὰς φίλας καὶ γείτονας λέγουσα Συνχάρητέ μοι, ὅτι εὗρον τὴν δραχμὴν ἣν ἀπώλεσα.
15:9.targetText: And when she finds it, she calls together her friends and neighbors to say, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost coin.’

groups.note: The relative clause ἣν ἀπώλεσα (which I lost) is rendered by the adjective lost.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for finds; the Greek participle has none.

15:10.sourceText: οὕτως, λέγω ὑμῖν, γίνεται χαρὰ ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐπὶ ἑνὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ μετανοοῦντι.
15:10.targetText: In the same way, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of God’s angels over one sinner who repents.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:11.sourceText: Εἶπεν δέ Ἄνθρωπός τις εἶχεν δύο υἱούς.
15:11.targetText: Then Jesus said, “There was a man who had two sons.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject that the Greek verb ending implies.
English supplies a presentational frame with no Greek counterpart.

15:12.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ νεώτερος αὐτῶν τῷ πατρί Πάτερ, δός μοι τὸ ἐπιβάλλον μέρος τῆς οὐσίας. ὁ δὲ διεῖλεν αὐτοῖς τὸν βίον.
15:12.targetText: The younger son said to him, ‘Father, give me my share of the estate.’ So he divided his property between them.

groups.note: The substantival ὁ νεώτερος (the younger one) is rendered The younger son.
τῷ πατρί (to the father) is rendered to him.
τὸ ἐπιβάλλον μέρος (the share that falls to me) is rendered my share.
The dative αὐτοῖς (to them) is rendered between them.
The article τόν is rendered as the possessive his.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not rendered; BSB starts a new sentence.
αὐτῶν (of them) is not separately expressed.

15:13.sourceText: καὶ μετ’ οὐ πολλὰς ἡμέρας συναγαγὼν πάντα ὁ νεώτερος υἱὸς ἀπεδήμησεν εἰς χώραν μακράν, καὶ ἐκεῖ διεσκόρπισεν τὴν οὐσίαν αὐτοῦ ζῶν ἀσώτως.
15:13.targetText: After a few days, the younger son got everything together and journeyed to a distant country, where he squandered his wealth in wild living.

groups.note: The litotes οὐ πολλάς (not many) is rendered a few.
συναγαγών (having gathered) is rendered got … together.
καὶ ἐκεῖ (and there) is rendered where.
The adverb ἀσώτως (recklessly) is rendered in wild, with living for ζῶν.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not rendered; BSB starts a new sentence.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle clause to the main verb.

15:14.sourceText: δαπανήσαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ πάντα ἐγένετο λιμὸς ἰσχυρὰ κατὰ τὴν χώραν ἐκείνην, καὶ αὐτὸς ἤρξατο ὑστερεῖσθαι.
15:14.targetText: After he had spent all he had, a severe famine swept through that country, and he began to be in need.

groups.note: The genitive absolute δαπανήσαντος … αὐτοῦ supplies the After-clause.
ἐγένετο (there came) is rendered swept, with through for κατά.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed; After belongs to the genitive absolute.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English completes all with he had; the Greek has only πάντα (everything).

15:15.sourceText: καὶ πορευθεὶς ἐκολλήθη ἑνὶ τῶν πολιτῶν τῆς χώρας ἐκείνης, καὶ ἔπεμψεν αὐτὸν εἰς τοὺς ἀγροὺς αὐτοῦ βόσκειν χοίρους·
15:15.targetText: So he went and hired himself out to a citizen of that country, who sent him into his fields to feed the pigs.

groups.note: The passive ἐκολλήθη (joined himself) is rendered hired himself out.
The καί clause is rendered as a relative clause; the citizen is the subject of sent.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle clause to the main verb.

15:16.sourceText: καὶ ἐπεθύμει γεμίσαι τὴν κοιλίαν αὐτοῦ ἐκ τῶν κερατίων ὧν ἤσθιον οἱ χοῖροι, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδίδου αὐτῷ.
15:16.targetText: He longed to fill his belly with the pods the pigs were eating, but no one would give him a thing.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not rendered; BSB starts a new sentence.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The relative ὧν (which) is left unexpressed in English.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for give; the Greek has none.

15:17.sourceText: εἰς ἑαυτὸν δὲ ἐλθὼν ἔφη Πόσοι μίσθιοι τοῦ πατρός μου περισσεύονται ἄρτων, ἐγὼ δὲ λιμῷ ὧδε ἀπόλλυμαι.
15:17.targetText: Finally he came to his senses and said, ‘How many of my father’s hired servants have plenty of food? But here I am, starving to death!

groups.note: ἑαυτόν (himself) in the idiom came to himself is rendered his senses.
BSB renders the connective δέ as Finally.
Πόσοι (how many) is rendered How many of before the possessive phrase.
ἄρτων (of bread) is rendered of food.
λιμῷ (by hunger) with ἀπόλλυμαι (I am perishing) is rendered starving to death.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle clause to the main verb.

15:18.sourceText: ἀναστὰς πορεύσομαι πρὸς τὸν πατέρα μου καὶ ἐρῶ αὐτῷ Πάτερ, ἥμαρτον εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐνώπιόν σου,
15:18.targetText: I will get up and go back to my father and say to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.

groups.note: ἐνώπιον (before) is rendered against.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle clause to the main verb.

15:19.sourceText: οὐκέτι εἰμὶ ἄξιος κληθῆναι υἱός σου· ποίησόν με ὡς ἕνα τῶν μισθίων σου.
15:19.targetText: I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired servants.”’

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:20.sourceText: καὶ ἀναστὰς ἦλθεν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα ἑαυτοῦ. ἔτι δὲ αὐτοῦ μακρὰν ἀπέχοντος εἶδεν αὐτὸν ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη, καὶ δραμὼν ἐπέπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ κατεφίλησεν αὐτόν.
15:20.targetText: So he got up and went to his father. But while he was still in the distance, his father saw him and was filled with compassion. He ran to his son, embraced him, and kissed him.

groups.note: μακράν (far off) is rendered in the distance.
The genitive absolute ἀπέχοντος (being away) supplies while … was.
ἐπέπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον (fell on the neck) is rendered embraced.
αὐτοῦ (his, of the neck) is rendered him.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
This καί is not rendered; BSB starts a new sentence.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle clause to the main verb.
English supplies the goal of ran; the participle δραμών has none.

15:21.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτῷ Πάτερ, ἥμαρτον εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐνώπιόν σου, οὐκέτι εἰμὶ ἄξιος κληθῆναι υἱός σου.
15:21.targetText: The son declared, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’

groups.note: ἐνώπιον (before) is rendered against.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The dative αὐτῷ (to him) is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:22.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ πατὴρ πρὸς τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ Ταχὺ ἐξενέγκατε στολὴν τὴν πρώτην καὶ ἐνδύσατε αὐτόν, καὶ δότε δακτύλιον εἰς τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ καὶ ὑποδήματα εἰς τοὺς πόδας,
15:22.targetText: But the father said to his servants, ‘Quick! Bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.

groups.note: πρώτην (first) is rendered best.
ἐνδύσατε (clothe) is rendered put … on.
χεῖρα (hand) is rendered finger, where the ring is worn.
The article τούς is rendered as the possessive his.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
This καί is not rendered; BSB starts a new sentence.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the robe as object; ἐνδύσατε has him as its object.

15:23.sourceText: καὶ φέρετε τὸν μόσχον τὸν σιτευτόν, θύσατε, καὶ φαγόντες εὐφρανθῶμεν,
15:23.targetText: Bring the fattened calf and kill it. Let us feast and celebrate.

groups.note: The participle φαγόντες (having eaten) is rendered feast.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not rendered; BSB starts a new sentence.
This καί is not rendered; BSB starts a new sentence.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the two commands; the Greek has no connective.
English supplies an object for kill; the Greek has none.
English joins the participle clause to the main verb.

15:24.sourceText: ὅτι οὗτος ὁ υἱός μου νεκρὸς ἦν καὶ ἀνέζησεν, ἦν ἀπολωλὼς καὶ εὑρέθη. καὶ ἤρξαντο εὐφραίνεσθαι.
15:24.targetText: For this son of mine was dead and is alive again! He was lost and is found!’ So they began to celebrate.

groups.note: The aorist ἀνέζησεν (came back to life) is rendered is alive again.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:25.sourceText: ἦν δὲ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ὁ πρεσβύτερος ἐν ἀγρῷ· καὶ ὡς ἐρχόμενος ἤγγισεν τῇ οἰκίᾳ, ἤκουσεν συμφωνίας καὶ χορῶν,
15:25.targetText: Meanwhile the older son was in the field, and as he approached the house, he heard music and dancing.

groups.note: BSB renders the connective δέ as Meanwhile.
ἐρχόμενος ἤγγισεν (coming, he drew near) is rendered he approached.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB says the older son and leaves αὐτοῦ (his) unexpressed.

15:26.sourceText: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος ἕνα τῶν παίδων ἐπυνθάνετο τί ἂν εἴη ταῦτα.
15:26.targetText: So he called one of the servants and asked what was going on.

groups.note: τί ἂν εἴη ταῦτα (what these things might be) is rendered what was going on.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle clause to the main verb.

15:27.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὅτι Ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἥκει, καὶ ἔθυσεν ὁ πατήρ σου τὸν μόσχον τὸν σιτευτόν, ὅτι ὑγιαίνοντα αὐτὸν ἀπέλαβεν.
15:27.targetText: ‘Your brother has returned,’ he said, ‘and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has him back safe and sound.’

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he.
ὑγιαίνοντα (being healthy) is rendered safe and sound.
ἀπέλαβεν (received back) is rendered has … back.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The dative αὐτῷ (to him) is not separately expressed.
ὅτι introduces the direct quotation and is represented by the quotation marks.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:28.sourceText: ὠργίσθη δὲ καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν εἰσελθεῖν· ὁ δὲ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ἐξελθὼν παρεκάλει αὐτόν.
15:28.targetText: The older son became angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.

groups.note: οὐκ ἤθελεν (was not willing) is rendered refused.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

English joins the participle clause to the main verb.

15:29.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν τῷ πατρὶ Ἰδοὺ τοσαῦτα ἔτη δουλεύω σοι καὶ οὐδέποτε ἐντολήν σου παρῆλθον, καὶ ἐμοὶ οὐδέποτε ἔδωκας ἔριφον ἵνα μετὰ τῶν φίλων μου εὐφρανθῶ·
15:29.targetText: But he answered his father, ‘Look, all these years I have served you and never disobeyed a commandment of yours. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he.
ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν (answering, said) is rendered answered.
τοσαῦτα (so many) is rendered all these.
The present δουλεύω with a span of years is rendered have served.
παρῆλθον (passed by, transgressed) is rendered disobeyed.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here; N1904 has only the article.
English adds even for emphasis; the Greek has no word for it.

15:30.sourceText: ὅτε δὲ ὁ υἱός σου οὗτος ὁ καταφαγών σου τὸν βίον μετὰ πορνῶν ἦλθεν, ἔθυσας αὐτῷ τὸν σιτευτὸν μόσχον.
15:30.targetText: But when this son of yours returns from squandering your wealth with prostitutes, you kill the fattened calf for him!’

groups.note: ὁ καταφαγών (the one who devoured) is rendered squandering.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:31.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Τέκνον, σὺ πάντοτε μετ’ ἐμοῦ εἶ, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐμὰ σά ἐστιν·
15:31.targetText: ‘Son, you are always with me,’ the father said, ‘and all that is mine is yours.

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he; BSB names the father.
Τέκνον (child) is rendered Son.
τὰ ἐμά (the things of mine) is rendered that … mine.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The dative αὐτῷ (to him) is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb of the relative clause.

15:32.sourceText: εὐφρανθῆναι δὲ καὶ χαρῆναι ἔδει, ὅτι ὁ ἀδελφός σου οὗτος νεκρὸς ἦν καὶ ἔζησεν, καὶ ἀπολωλὼς καὶ εὑρέθη.
15:32.targetText: But it was fitting to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’”

groups.note: ἦν is understood again with ἀπολωλώς.
The aorist ἔζησεν (came to life) is rendered is alive again.
